meta.triageRationale: One module (the review host's createPanel in extension.ts) and one obvious approach; vscode.window.tabGroups is already used. One small design choice for the LLD: which group when several qualify, and whether the pane takes focus when the chat opens it.

findings.premise: The design covers the request (reuse an existing non-chat group; otherwise today's placement; quiet opens keep focus in the chat) and builds no non-goal (other panels such as the delivery board stay at ViewColumn.Active).

summary.prose: When the review pane opens, it now goes into an editor group you already have open, as long as that group is not the one holding the chat, instead of opening beside or over the chat. If there is no other group open, it opens exactly where it does today: a new group beside the chat when the chat opened it for a document it presents, and the active group when you opened it yourself from the command or the delivery board. A pane the chat opens on a presented document still does not take your cursor.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Open the review pane in an existing editor group, not beside the chat

dataModelChanges.entity: chooseReviewColumn (new vscode-free function in vscode-plugin/src/chat/review-column.ts, beside group-lock.ts)
dataModelChanges.details: chooseReviewColumn(groups: readonly { readonly viewColumn: number; readonly isActive: boolean; readonly tabs: readonly { readonly input: unknown }[] }[], chatViewType: string): number | undefined. It leaves out every group with a tab satisfying isChatTabInput(input, chatViewType). Among the rest it returns the active group's viewColumn when the active group is one of them, otherwise the lowest viewColumn; it returns undefined when no group is left. It reads nothing from vscode and never throws.
callSites: vscode-plugin/src/extension.ts (the review host's createPanel callback reads vscode.window.tabGroups.all into the plain list and uses the result)

dataModelChanges.details: Today the pane is created at ViewColumn.Beside with preserveFocus (quiet, a document the chat presents) or ViewColumn.Active (the command and the board), which puts it beside the chat's group or in the active group, which may be the chat's. After the change both paths first use the column chooseReviewColumn returns (a group holding no chat tab); when it returns undefined or reading the groups fails, each path keeps today's placement: ViewColumn.Beside with preserveFocus when quiet, ViewColumn.Active otherwise. Two source-scan tests in review-wiring.test.ts that pin the current calls are rewritten with it.

The plugin builds against a local compile-only shim of the vscode module, which today declares only TabGroup.activeTab and TabGroups.activeTabGroup, onDidChangeTabs and onDidChangeTabGroups. The change needs TabGroups to gain `readonly all: readonly TabGroup[]` and TabGroup to gain `readonly viewColumn: ViewColumn`, `readonly isActive: boolean` and `readonly tabs: readonly Tab[]`, matching the real vscode API, so extension.ts typechecks.

An already open pane is only revealed.
migration.stateAfter: A new review pane is created in an open editor group that holds no chat tab (the active one when it qualifies, else the lowest column); when there is none it opens as it does today (beside the chat when quiet, the active group otherwise). A quiet open keeps preserveFocus. An already open pane is revealed as before.

alternativesConsidered.name: A vscode-free placement function over the tab groups
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A small pure function takes the open tab groups and the chat's view type and returns the column to use, or none; extension.ts passes the result to createWebviewPanel.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A new vscode-free function in the plugin (next to group-lock.ts, reusing its isChatTabInput rule) takes a plain list of groups { viewColumn, isActive, tabs[].input } and the chat view type. It leaves out every group that holds a tab satisfying isChatTabInput. Among the rest it picks the active group when it is one of them, otherwise the first by column; with no such group it returns undefined. The review host's createPanel in extension.ts reads vscode.window.tabGroups.all into that plain list, and uses the returned column, or, when the function returns undefined, today's placement (ViewColumn.Beside when quiet, ViewColumn.Active otherwise). A quiet open (the chat's presenter) keeps preserveFocus. Only the review pane is changed.
pros: The rule is testable with fake groups, like group-lock.ts, instead of a source scan
Reuses the one definition of 'this tab is the chat'
Falls back to today's behaviour on both paths when no other group is open
A few lines in extension.ts: reading the groups and passing the column
cons: A group that holds only other webviews or an unrelated editor is also reused, so the pane becomes one more tab there
Which group to choose when several qualify (active, else first) is a convention, not something the user states

alternativesConsidered.name: The same rule written inline in extension.ts
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: extension.ts scans tabGroups and picks a column in the createPanel callback, with no separate module.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The createPanel callback reads vscode.window.tabGroups.all, finds the groups without a chat tab (using isChatTabInput), picks the active one or the first, and passes its viewColumn to createWebviewPanel, falling back to today's placement (Beside when quiet, Active otherwise).
cons: extension.ts imports vscode and cannot run in tests, so the rule can only be pinned by a source scan, which proves nothing about which group is chosen
Grows an already large activate function
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Same behaviour at lower cost, but the rule that is the whole change cannot be tested: only a source scan could pin it.

alternativesConsidered.name: A fixed column or a remembered column
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Open the pane in a fixed column (for example Two) or in the column the previous review pane used.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Use ViewColumn.Two always, or remember the column of the last review pane and reuse it when its group still exists and is not the chat's.
pros: Very little code for the fixed column
A remembered column keeps the pane where the user last put it
cons: A fixed column ignores the user's layout and can be the chat's own group, which is the thing to avoid
A remembered column adds state that must be kept in step with groups that are closed or reordered
Neither reuses a group the user already has open
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Does not meet the request: it ignores the user's layout.

openQuestions: cd1 (partial): chooseReviewColumn is a new function this Story introduces; it is labelled new in dataModel and is not an existing symbol.
ts1 (partial): the Story carries no acceptance criteria; ac1-ac3 in the test mapping are derived from the request, not stated by the owner.
alt2 (partial): the alternatives are scored against the request and testability only; the Story has no formal constraints, HLD contracts or Epic constraints.

OWNER DECISION: when several groups other than the chat's are open, which one should the pane use? This LLD's choice: the active group if it is not the chat's, otherwise the one with the lowest column. Alternative: always the group that held the most recently active non-chat editor. Recommendation: keep the choice as written.

DECIDED IN THE LLD (change to confirm): when no other group is open, the non-quiet path (the command and the delivery board) keeps ViewColumn.Active, as today; only a quiet open falls back to Beside, as today. No fallback changes.
